title: Define interactive ink and elevation kinetics for compact controls
creator: Ava Morales
description:
Goal: Create a cohesive, accessible set of design tokens and interaction rules for 'compact' controls (buttons, chips, table rows, compact cards) that unify color/ink behavior, elevation/shadow kinetics, spacing/radius trade-offs, and typography adjustments.

Scope:
- Define a small token surface for interactive ink (hover/pressed/drag) tuned for high-density UIs.
- Establish elevation kinetics: micro-elevation values and motion patterns for press/release and focus transitions.
- Provide clear migration guidance for components that will adopt compact tokens (buttons, primary/secondary actions, table row hover/selection, compact chart legend chips).
- Ensure tokens meet WCAG contrast for all interaction states and adapt across light/dark themes.

Deliverables:
1) Token catalog (color swatches, ink overlays, elevation steps, radius presets, compact type scale).
2) Interaction motion spec (timings: press / release / hover / focus, easing curves).
3) Component mappings (which token to use per component/state).
4) Migration plan, deprecation notes, and rollout checklist.

Why now: Compact mode adoption across the console has grown; existing token granularity causes visual noise and inconsistent press feedback in dense tables and action bars. This work reduces token sprawl while improving perceived responsiveness and accessibility for keyboard/touch users.
acceptance_criteria: Token set published in the tokens repo with semantic names and examples in Figma
Motion spec documented with timing and easing; prototype shows press/release kinetics for a button and table row
Hand-off checklist completed and at least 3 core components migrated in a single PR with visual regression screenshots
Contrast checks (automated) show all interactive foregrounds on token backgrounds meet WCAG AA for normal text or provide compensating semantics
Developer guide added: migration path, fallback tokens, and feature flag for gradual rollout
decisions: Favor semantic tokens (ink-compact-*) instead of color-based tokens to allow runtime theming and A/B of elevation intensity
Use shallow elevation steps for compact mode to reduce perceived blockiness in dense lists
Prefer subtle ink overlays for press state on primary/secondary buttons in compact mode to keep width/height stable
Motion durations: press = 80ms, release = 160ms, hover fade = 120ms; easing = cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)
Keep two radius presets for compact: 6px for tight controls, 8px for slightly raised elements

notes: Migration recommendation: add feature flag 'compact-tokens' to enable staged rollout; ship tokens behind flag and migrate actions first (buttons/chips) before table rows
Follow-up: run a short usability study with keyboard-only users to verify focus ring visibility and elevation cues in compact mode
Risk: aggressive alpha for ink overlays on dark themes can trip contrast; create theme-specific token overrides when needed
